title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Link-Copying, Pattern-Entropy, and Distinct-Vertex Blow-Up Certificates for Uniform Hypergraphs
abstract: Dhruv Mubayi (arXiv:2611.33108, November 23, 2026) proved that every sufficiently large n-vertex k-uniform hypergraph containing at least a n^h copies of a fixed h-vertex k-graph H contains a blow-up H[t] with parts of optimal order t >= b(log n)^{1/(k-1)} (Theorem 1 and Corollary 2), resolving a question of Rodl and Schacht, proving the 1976 conjecture of Bollobas, Erdos, and Simonovits, and answering Erdos's 1990 $500 Ramsey prize problem for all k >= 4 via almost-monochromatic sets of density >= 1 - alpha (Corollary 3). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Q certificate auditor for the algebraic, link-copying, pattern-entropy, and distinct-vertex core of these results. An 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (HypergraphBlowup.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 6 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes 3- and 4-partite link-copying telescoping S_{h,a_h}...S_{1,a_1} J, idempotence and monotonicity, inductive Eq. (10) pattern-count sums, exact triangle (12t^2) and tetrahedron (32t^3) entropy exponents at s=2t, cleared integer AM-GM and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities, s=2t distinct-vertex halving, optimal exponent degree balance t^{k-1}*t = t^k, and cleared Corollary 3 almost-monochromatic density inequalities for k=3,4. HYPERGRAPH-BLOWUP-CERT-1.0 audits four exact-Q modes across 16 canonical certificates (0.032-4.136 ms) and rejects 60/60 live adversarial forgeries.
